answer: An agent economy can make each account post a refundable bond before it may place orders, with the bond locked until a dispute window closes. If an account is caught double-spending or violating the market’s rules, a verifier can slash the bond; otherwise it is returned. Creating a thousand identities therefore requires a thousand funded bonds, not just a thousand usernames, and the attacker risks losing capital as well as paying the opportunity cost of leaving it locked. A juniper seller on the tundra cannot cheaply gain influence by multiplying accounts at the ledge.
